SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF WESTBROOK
COUNTY OF MARION

PEOPLE v. DANIEL R. ORTEGA            Case No. CR-2024-00871

DEFENDANT'S MOTION TO SUPPRESS STATEMENTS AND PHYSICAL EVIDENCE

Defendant, by and through counsel, moves this Court for an order suppressing:
(1) any statement made by Defendant after his unequivocal invocation of counsel at 00:11 on March 15, 2024, including the response to Officer Halberg's question "Where did you ditch the phone?" at 00:24 (Edwards v. Arizona, 451 U.S. 477 (1981)); and
(2) the folding knife recovered from Defendant's person, on grounds that the Terry frisk exceeded its lawful scope under Minnesota v. Dickerson, 508 U.S. 366 (1993).

GROUNDS:
1. The initial stop was supported only by a general clothing description ("dark grey hoodie, blue jeans") shared by a substantial portion of the local population at that hour. Defendant was wearing a black hoodie and dark pants — colors that do not match the description in the dispatch call.

2. The victim's show-up identification was qualified ("I think that's him, but I'm not 100% sure") and conducted under suggestive single-suspect conditions in violation of the standards in Neil v. Biggers, 409 U.S. 188 (1972).

3. Officer Bell's body-worn camera was inoperative for the duration of the stop (see Arrest Report, Evidence Item 3). The People will be unable to corroborate Officer Halberg's account of Defendant's alleged movement toward his pocket — the act on which the frisk's escalation depends.

4. Defendant unequivocally invoked his right to counsel at 00:11. Officer Halberg's renewed question at 00:24 was a violation of Edwards. Any answer, including the denial ("I don't know what you're talking about"), must be suppressed.

WHEREFORE, Defendant respectfully requests this Court grant the relief sought.

Dated: April 18, 2024
                                /s/ M. Tran, Esq.
                                Marion County Public Defender's Office
